fathom

This is the living specification for the package. It describes what the package is, what it does and does not do, and why each of those is the way it is.

It serves two readers. Someone who wants to know why a decision was made, and a future session of Claude that needs both the whole shape and the granular reasoning. Sections 1 through 4 describe the package as the code stands and are regenerated from the code rather than carried forward, so where they and a help page disagree, the help page and the code win. Sections 5 and 6 are the reasoning and the evidence the code cannot supply. Section 7 is how to work on it. Section 8 is what remains open, and section 9 is the multimodal design and what it took to settle.

Almost every decision in section 5 reads as a defect from outside. That section exists so it does not have to be re-argued.

1. What the package is

fathom annotates a corpus with a language model served locally by Ollama. Every document is put to one or more questions, and each answer is read from the probability distribution over the first token the model generates. The text the model writes is never parsed.

That distribution is the whole measurement. ollama_generate() in R/backend.R asks for one generated token with log probabilities on and up to 20 alternatives in top_logprobs. score_labels() in R/score.R turns the returned list into one row per label. A token counts toward a label when it opens one of that label’s strings, or equals one under exact matching, and the probabilities of the tokens counting toward a label are summed. What lands on no label is prob_other, and the label probabilities rescaled to sum to one are prob_renorm. Prefix matching is the reason instrument() refuses two labels that share a first character unless exact = TRUE.

The rest of the package sits on either side of that call. R/prepare.R turns images, recordings and videos into data frames measure() can read. R/audit.R describes how items behaved and draws samples for people to code, and R/validate.R scores the model against those codings and the coders against each other.

2. Current shape

Everything in this section is counted or copied from the files in the tree.

NAMESPACE exports seventeen functions and registers six S3 methods. Those are measure.character, measure.data.frame, and print for fathom_backend, fathom_instrument, fathom_results and fathom_validation. The only import is %>% from magrittr. 2.2 Internal helpers worth knowing

Helper File What it does
build_prompt() R/prompt.R Joins the document block, the question, the cue and the answer marker. An empty document string drops the document block.
prompt_hash(), item_hashes() R/hash.R One 12-character md5 prefix per item over the question, cue, text_label, answer_label, label names and strings, model, and whether the run has a text column.
ckpt_path(), ckpt_read(), ckpt_write(), ckpt_stale() R/checkpoint.R One .rds per document, written to a temporary file and renamed, and the rule for which items still need a call.
resolve_num_ctx(), ckpt_num_ctx() R/context.R Turns the num_ctx argument into an integer or NULL, measuring it under "auto".
ollama_generate() R/backend.R The only function that posts to /api/generate. Scoring calls, the num_ctx probe, label probing and check_backend() all go through it.
ollama_tags(), show_models(), ollama_modalities() R/backend.R The model list from /api/tags, and per-model capabilities from /api/show for the printed listing only.
normalize_host() R/backend.R A host read the way Ollama’s own client reads OLLAMA_HOST, with http:// added where no scheme was given and port 11434 where no port was either.
check_backend() R/backend.R The check measure() runs before any document, with nine paths returning FALSE. Not exported, and called directly by data-raw/bake_results.R.
probe_labels() R/instrument.R One call per label, recording the first emitted token in firsts and adding it to normalized.
default_cue(), choice_listing(), reorder_labels() R/instrument.R The cue instrument() writes when none is given, the listing under an exclusive question, and the same instrument with its labels shown in another order, which is what order_sensitivity() sends.
score_labels(), match_token(), logsumexp() R/score.R A top-k list to one row per label.
apply_scores() R/score.R Recomputes expected_score from prob_renorm and the scores of the instrument passed in.
measure_one(), measure_doc(), fail_rows() R/measure.R One call, every stale item for one document, and the failure rows whose columns define the flat schema.
new_results() R/measure.R Splits the flat frame into $probs and $calls using PROB_COLS, CALL_COLS and DROP_COLS.
reserved_cols(), probe_doc(), restrict_items() R/measure.R The names keep may not use, the document check_backend() is sent, and the filter that returns only the requested items.
winning_rows() R/utils.R The winning row of each call, and no row for a call whose distribution held none of the labels.
flat_results() R/utils.R Joins $probs to chosen $calls columns for functions that need both grains.
as_docs(), as_media() R/utils.R Documents as id and .fathom_text, and media as a list of path vectors.
stamp_provenance() R/utils.R Attaches run_at, and call when given.
local_seed() R/utils.R Seeds the random stream for the calling function and puts the session’s stream back when that function exits. NULL leaves the stream alone.
check_conf_level() R/utils.R Refuses a coverage that is not a single number between 0 and 1.
check_bootstrap_n(), check_image_col() R/utils.R Refuses fewer than a hundred replicates, for validate_sample() and order_sensitivity(), and an image naming no column of docs, for coding_sample() and order_sensitivity().
check_target() R/utils.R Refuses a target that names no label, for item_report(), inspect_cases() and threshold_sensitivity().
off_label(), call_diagnostics() R/audit.R Whether an emitted token matched no label under the scoring rule, and the item-level columns all three item_report() shapes share.
allocate_budget(), pps_draw() R/audit.R The split across items and the systematic draw behind coding_sample().
validate_many() R/validate.R The path validate_sample() takes for a list of sheets.
merge_sheets(), finish_reference() R/validate.R The full join of coder sheets, and the provenance stamped on a reference sheet.
read_sheet() R/validate.R A sheet given as a path, read with every column as text and human_prop turned back into a number.
kripp_parts(), delta_squared() R/validate.R Krippendorff’s alpha with its expected and observed disagreement, and the ordinal difference function.
resample_units(), ci_percentile() R/validate.R Row resampling, and the percentile interval read off it.
coder_agreement(), gap_table() R/validate.R The ceiling and the gap behind $ceiling and $gap. Internal, since only the several-sheet path calls them.

labels_from_instrument() R/validate.R Label order by scores, used as the ordinal scale.
cache_state(), read_timings(), pick_frames() R/prepare.R Whether a transcript on disk matches the requested settings, word timings as a table, and the times frames are taken at.
scene_scores(), scene_lines() R/prepare.R ffmpeg’s score for every frame, read off its log rather than out of a file.

The constants in R/ are the stem tables ITEM_STEMS, CHOICE_STEMS, STEM_MEDIA and LANG_PRESETS in R/instrument.R, the schema vectors ITEM_COLS, PROB_COLS, DROP_COLS and CALL_COLS in R/measure.R, TAGS_TIMEOUT in R/backend.R, and ALL_ITEMS, the pooled row label "(all items)", in R/validate.R.

2.4 Objects that travel between functions

These are the shapes one function builds and another reads. Field and column names are listed in the order the code creates them.

fathom_backend

ollama_backend() builds a list of eight fields, model, keep_alive, timeout, think, top_logprobs, host, modalities and validated. It holds no connection, and think is always FALSE, with no argument to set it. modalities takes text, image or both. instrument() hands it to probe_labels(), measure() reads modalities and passes the object to ollama_generate(), every checkpoint payload stores it, and results carry it as the backend attribute.

fathom_instrument

instrument() builds a list of sixteen fields, items, labels, normalized, cue, text_label, answer_label, lang, exclusive, exact_match, definitions, scores, probe_texts, firsts, k, n_items and name. labels and normalized are named lists keyed by label, scores is stored in label order, and firsts stays NULL until probe_labels() records a token for every label. An exclusive instrument has one item named category, whose text is the question followed by one name = description line per label. build_prompt() reads items, cue, text_label and answer_label. score_labels() reads labels, normalized, exact_match and scores. prompt_hash() reads the same fields as build_prompt() apart from the document, plus the label names and strings.

The flat frame

measure_doc() returns this frame and the loop in measure.data.frame() completes it. Its columns are id, any keep columns, item, prompt_hash, model, label, logprob, prob, prob_renorm, present, top1_token, top1_prob, prob_other, entropy, margin, expected_score, winner, call_ok, error, prompt_tokens, prefill_ms, wall_ms, truncated and all_absent. fail_rows() produces the same columns from label onward with call_ok = FALSE. Checkpoints store this frame and results do not.

Checkpoint payload

There is one file per document at ckpt_path(id, dir). The file name is the id with every character outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] replaced by an underscore and cut to 96 characters, then a hyphen, the first 8 characters of the md5 of the id, and .rds. The payload is a list of id, instrument, backend, num_ctx, run_at and results. num_ctx is NA_integer_ for a run with no ceiling, and results holds the flat frame for every item that document has held.

fathom_results

new_results() returns list(probs, calls) with class fathom_results and attributes instrument, backend, model, num_ctx, exclusive and run_at. $probs holds PROB_COLS, which are id, item, label and prob_renorm. $calls holds one row per id and item with CALL_COLS, which are id, item, error, truncated, top1_token, prob_other, margin, expected_score and prompt_hash, followed by any keep columns. DROP_COLS are entropy, logprob, prefill_ms, prompt_tokens, wall_ms, winner, model, prob, present, call_ok, top1_prob and all_absent, and they stop at this point. measure.character() adds a docs attribute holding the documents as a named character vector, and read_checkpoints() replaces run_at.

flat_results(x, cols) left-joins $probs to the requested $calls columns on id and item and copies the attributes instrument, backend, model, exclusive, num_ctx, run_at and docs. as_wide(), inspect_cases(), item_report(), threshold_sensitivity(), coding_sample() and validate_sample() each start by calling it.

Coding sheet

coding_sample() returns a tibble with columns id, item, question, allowed, human_label, note, text and image. Its class is reset to tbl_df, and its attribute is run_at. human_label and note come back NA for the coder. image holds one path, or a video window’s frame paths joined in order with |.

Reference sheet

coder_reference() returns id, item, human_label, n_coders and n_agree. Under method = "soft" it returns id, item, human_prop, human_target, n_coders and n_target instead. The attributes are run_at and call.

fathom_validation

On one label sheet, validate_sample() returns a list of discrimination and categories, plus calibration under calibration = TRUE and coded under coded = TRUE. A soft sheet returns calibration whatever the switch says, and coded on request. $discrimination has item, n, agreement and alpha, one row per question plus (all items). $categories has item, label, n, precision, recall and auc, one row per label per question with no pooled row. $calibration has item, n, and brier or rps. $coded is the sheet with model_label, one prob_renorm column per label, correct, and brier or rps added. The attributes are level, conf_level, n_coded, run_at and call.

On a list of sheets it adds ceiling and gap, puts a coder column after item in the stacked tables, stacks $coded one row per coder when asked, and adds the attribute coders. $ceiling is a plain list of alpha, with item, n_units and alpha, and pairs, with coder_a, coder_b, item, n, agreement and alpha. $gap has item, n, model_alpha, coder_alpha, gap and gap_ci, one row per question.

Prepared corpora

prepare_image() returns id, image, bytes, exists and ext. prepare_audio() returns id, audio, exists, text, duration_s, n_words, n_turns, n_speakers, n_pauses, n_gaps, median_gap_s, speech_rate, articulation_rate, median_turn_s, median_score, diarized, annotate_timing, transcribed, tool, asr_model, language, min_pause and extra. prepare_video() binds those columns to video, has_audio, image, n_frames, frame_times, select, include_first, scene_median and scene_max, with image and frame_times as list columns. On disk, prepare_audio() reads or writes <stem>.json with a settings record in <stem>.fathom.json, and prepare_video() writes <stem>_frames/<stem>_fNN.jpg and <stem>.wav, beside each recording unless cache_dir is given. The frames keep their own record, <stem>_frames.fathom.json, of the times they were cut at and the JPEG quality, and a set cut under anything else is removed and cut again. find_ffprobe() looks for ffprobe beside the ffmpeg in use, then on the PATH, and refuses when neither has it.

Shipped data and baked results

R/data.R documents two datasets, parlasent with 100 rows and 19 columns and ati with 300 and 5. data-raw/bake_results.R runs against gemma4:31b, checkpoints under data-raw/cache, and saves the objects the vignettes and help-page examples read to inst/extdata/vignette_results.rds, which are res_six, res_topics, res_indep and order_six. order_six is cached under data-raw/cache beside the checkpoints, named for res_six’s prompt hash and marked all for an audit of every document, since order_sensitivity() keeps no checkpoint of its own.

3. The measurement path

This follows a data frame and an instrument to a fathom_results object. The backend and the instrument exist before measure() is called, so their construction comes first.

3.1 Before measure()

  1. ollama_backend() checks its arguments locally, caps top_logprobs at 20 with a warning, and takes the host from host, then OLLAMA_HOST, then localhost on port 11434, through normalize_host(). An empty OLLAMA_HOST counts as unset, and a host with no scheme and no port is given port 11434, both the way Ollama’s own client reads it. With validate = FALSE it builds the object and returns. Otherwise it calls ollama_tags(). A failed request, an empty model list, a missing model name and a name absent from the list all stop, and the last two print the listing through show_models() first.
  2. template_items() is optional. It resolves a preset name through stem_lookup() in ITEM_STEMS by lang and medium, or takes a string containing {label}, and returns one question per category.
  3. instrument() refuses anything in ..., refuses exact = TRUE without backend, and refuses a list passed as labels. An exclusive instrument then resolves its one question through stem_lookup() in CHOICE_STEMS, renames the item category, refuses labels carrying text when there are no definitions, appends one name = definition line per label, and builds its cue from cue_fmt_one. An unnamed character vector of items is named Q1, Q2 and so on, and items must then be named, unique, non-empty strings. Labels must be at least two unique, non-empty strings with no whitespace, tested through stringi. normalized is each label passed through trimws() and stri_trans_toupper(), and two labels normalizing to one string are refused. Unless exact = TRUE, two labels sharing a first character are refused. definitions and probe_texts pass through check_label_map(), scores must name every label and are reordered to match labels, and a missing cue is built from cue_fmt and paste_or().
  4. When backend is given, instrument() ends with probe_labels(). It sends one prompt per label, built by build_prompt() from the first item and either that label’s probe_texts entry or the sentence “This text is entirely and exclusively about” followed by the label’s description or name. It calls ollama_generate() with no ceiling and reads the first returned token. If any label gets no token back, a warning is raised and the instrument is returned unprobed. A token that is not a prefix of its own label’s strings stops construction, and so do two labels returning the same token. Otherwise each token is added to that label’s normalized strings and all of them are recorded in firsts.
  5. preview() prints build_prompt() for one item, the table of normalized strings per label, any scores, and the probe result, and makes no call.

3.2 measure() up to the first document

  1. measure.character() puts the vector in a tibble with .id, taken from the names or the positions, and .text. It calls the data frame method and attaches the documents to the result as the docs attribute.
  2. measure.data.frame() refuses anything in ..., matches verbosity, names a backend and instrument passed the other way round, and checks the classes of instrument and backend. It then requires text or image to be named and to exist in x, requires backend$modalities to include each of text and image that was named, requires the id and keep columns to exist, refuses keep names from reserved_cols() and repeated keep names, refuses items names that are not items, and refuses repeated ids.
  3. item_hashes() computes one hash per item, with has_text true when text was named, and the hashes are cut to the items in items. Documents become "" when no text column was named, and the media column is passed through as_media().
  4. resolve_num_ctx() settles the ceiling. A checkpoint directory that already holds a payload with num_ctx decides it, through ckpt_num_ctx(). Otherwise NULL or NA gives no ceiling, a number below 512 is refused and any other number is used, and a string other than "auto" is refused. Under "auto", fewer than two documents with no media gives no ceiling. The remaining case sends one prompt through ollama_generate() with no ceiling, built from the longest document by word count, or the document with the most media bytes, and the longest question. The ceiling is the next power of two at or above 1.25 times the returned prompt_eval_count, and never below 2048. A count of at least 2048 that is no more than 8 above a multiple of 1024 adds a note to the message. A failed probe or a missing count warns and gives no ceiling.
  5. The run header prints unless verbosity = "quiet", and a warning is raised when checkpointing is off and documents times items exceeds 2000. Its values start at HEADER_WIDTH. The Context Ceiling line gives the ceiling alone, with (from the saved run) when a checkpoint decided it, and the Longest doc line gives the document’s id, words and tokens.
  6. check_backend() runs with the instrument, the resolved ceiling, images set when a media column was named, and the text from probe_doc(), which is the non-empty document nearest the median word count. With no usable text it sends a built-in weather question and ignores the instrument’s items. It returns FALSE at the first failure. Before any request it fails an instrument with exact matching and no firsts. It then fails a tag request that errors, a server with no models, and a model missing from the list. After the probe call it fails a call that errors, a reply with no top_logprobs, and a first token that match_token() counts as no label. With media and a backend declaring image, it sends one red and one blue test image and fails when either call errors or the two distributions are identical. measure() stops on FALSE with “backend check failed. Not starting.”

3.3 The document loop

  1. For each row, ckpt_read() loads the previous payload when checkpointing is on. It returns NULL for a missing or unreadable file and for a payload whose stored id differs, and it renames an old ok column to call_ok. ckpt_stale() then lists the wanted items that have no row with call_ok true, the backend’s model and the current prompt hash.
  2. A document with nothing stale returns its stored rows cut to the wanted items by restrict_items(), with its keep columns read from x rather than off the payload, by the closure rekeep(). If checkpointing is on and the stored instrument’s scores differ from the current ones, the payload is rewritten with the current instrument and apply_scores(), with no call.
  3. A document with stale items goes to measure_doc(), which runs measure_one() for each of those items in instrument order and prepends item, prompt_hash and model to each block. The loop binds id and the row’s keep values in front, appends the stored rows for items not re-run with their keep columns read from x the same way, sorts by the instrument’s item order, writes the payload with ckpt_write(), and returns the rows cut by restrict_items(). A progress line prints after every tenth document that made calls, except on the last row.

3.4 One call

measure_one() builds the prompt with build_prompt(). With the English preset and a two-label instrument it reads as follows.

Text: "<document>"

<question>

Answer with exactly one word: YES or NO.

Answer:

The document block is left out when the document string is empty. ollama_generate() posts model, prompt, think, stream = FALSE, logprobs = TRUE, top_logprobs, keep_alive and options to /api/generate, with num_predict = 1, temperature = 0 and num_ctx when a ceiling is set. Media paths are read as raw bytes and sent base64-encoded in images. The elapsed time is added to the response as wall_ms.

score_labels() takes the top_logprobs list at position 1 and sorts it by log probability. Each token is trimmed and upper-cased through stringi. For each label, match_token() keeps the tokens that are non-empty and open one of the label’s normalized strings, or under exact_match the tokens equal to one. logsumexp() of their log probabilities gives logprob, which is -Inf when none matched, and prob is its exponential capped at 1. With total as the sum of prob over labels, prob_renorm is prob / total and prob_other is max(0, 1 - total). entropy, margin and expected_score are computed from prob_renorm, and winner is the label with the largest prob. prob_renorm, entropy, margin, expected_score and winner are all NA when total is 0. present is whether logprob is finite, and top1_token and top1_prob come from the first token of the sorted list.

measure_one() then adds call_ok = TRUE, error = NA, prompt_tokens from prompt_eval_count, prefill_ms from prompt_eval_duration, wall_ms, truncated and all_absent. truncated is NA with no ceiling and otherwise true when prompt_eval_count is within 64 tokens of num_ctx. all_absent is true when no label is present. A request error, a reply with no top_logprobs at position 1, or an error inside score_labels() returns fail_rows() instead, with the reason in error.

3.5 After the loop

  1. The per-document frames are bound, and apply_scores() recomputes expected_score against the instrument passed to measure(). It writes NA when the instrument has no scores and errors on a label that has no score. The run summary prints elapsed time, documents processed and skipped, and item failures counted as failed rows divided by the number of labels.
  2. new_results() builds the return value with a new structure(). It keeps PROB_COLS in $probs, keeps CALL_COLS and any column outside PROB_COLS and DROP_COLS in $calls on the first row per id and item, and attaches instrument, backend, model, num_ctx, exclusive and a fresh run_at. num_ctx is a required argument, the resolved ceiling as an integer or NA for none.

3.6 Reading a run back

read_checkpoints() reads every .rds in the directory, drops files that fail to read, and errors when none were found or none of them read. It binds their results, runs apply_scores() under the first payload’s instrument, and calls new_results() with that instrument, backend and num_ctx, which is NA when the payload has none. It then sets run_at to the latest stored stamp. Rows come back in directory-listing order.

4. The validation family

coding_sample(), validate_sample() and coder_reference() are the exported half. coder_agreement() and gap_table() are internal and run only inside the several-sheet path. This section covers what each object carries to the next function, what the functions share underneath, and which arrangement of calls answers which question. Arguments and return values are on the help pages.

4.1 What rides on a sheet

coding_sample() writes no design columns, since every pair has the same chance. A coder fills human_label. merge_sheets() requires that column with id and item, and validate_sample() requires it or human_prop. Any other column a sheet carries is read by nothing, which is how a sheet drawn before the draw went uniform-only still scores the same.

coder_reference() and coder_agreement() both pass their sheets through merge_sheets(), which names unnamed sheets coder1, coder2 and so on, refuses a coder named id or item, and full-joins on id and item. A sheet given as a path, here or to validate_sample(), is read by read_sheet() with every column as text, so an id of digits is neither rounded nor stripped of its leading zeros.

4.2 What each function reads from results

coding_sample() calls flat_results(results, c("error", "margin")), keeps calls with no error, takes the highest-prob_renorm row per id and item, and leaves out pairs whose margin or prob_renorm is NA before drawing.

validate_sample() calls flat_results(results, "error") and keeps calls with no error. It refuses repeated id, item and label rows, and any group whose prob_renorm does not sum to 1 within 1e-6. model_label is the highest-prob_renorm label per id and item, taken through winning_rows(), so a call whose distribution held none of the labels has none. prob_renorm is widened to one column per label, and both are inner-joined to the sheet on id and item, which sets a coded row with no model_label aside and says how many.

coder_agreement() and coder_reference() never see results. gap_table() reads id, item, model_label and n_coders from the union of the coders’ $coded, and every column of the ceiling’s merged frame other than id and item as a coder.

4.3 What they share

Every alpha comes from kripp_parts(), unweighted. Every bootstrap interval comes from resample_units() and ci_percentile(), which resample document-item rows with replacement. validate_sample() draws once per question and reads every figure for that question off the same draws, so turning calibration on changes no other interval. coder_agreement() draws once per item scope and reads $alpha and $pairs off the same draws. gap_table() recomputes both averages on the same rows in each replicate. All three seed the stream through local_seed() for the length of the call, 1234L by default. order_sensitivity() compares the model with itself rather than with a coder, so it sits outside the family, and it shares the same kripp_parts(), resample_units(), ci_percentile() and local_seed().

Both tables that pool label the pooled row "(all items)" from ALL_ITEMS and leave it out when there is one item. labels_from_instrument() turns an instrument’s scores into the ordinal scale. stamp_provenance() puts run_at on every object here, and call on all of them except the coding sheet.

4.4 The several-sheet path

validate_sample() sends any list that is not a data frame to validate_many(), which works in this order.

  1. It refuses fewer than two sheets and names unnamed sheets the way merge_sheets() does, and resolves labels from instrument once.
  2. It runs validate_sample() on every sheet with coded = TRUE, with messages suppressed after the first.
  3. It stacks each table across coders with a coder column after item.
  4. It calls coder_agreement() on the same sheets for $ceiling.
  5. It takes id, item, model_label and n_coders from every coder’s $coded, keeps one row per id and item, and hands that and the ceiling’s merged frame to gap_table(), which warns when n_coders is present.
  6. It stacks every coder’s $coded with a coder column only when coded is true, and stamps level, coders, conf_level, n_coded, run_at and call.

4.5 Arrangements

Arrangement Calls What it answers Where it stops or warns
The model against one coder validate_sample(sheet, results) how the model’s labels read against one person, overall and per label there is no ceiling, and a list holding one sheet is refused
The model against the coders validate_sample(list(a = a, b = b), results) the row above for each coder, how well the coders agreed, and whether the model agrees with them as well as they agree with each other refuses fewer than two sheets and sheets with no row coded by two coders
The model against a consensus validate_sample(coder_reference(a, b), results), with "majority" or "unanimous" the model against one reconciled label per row "majority" leaves ties blank, "unanimous" warns, and a consolidated sheet placed in a list warns
The model against a share of coders validate_sample(coder_reference(a, b, method = "soft"), results) the Brier score against the proportion of coders choosing human_target coder_reference() refuses more than two labels, and validate_sample() refuses a sheet with no human_target

5. Decisions that look like defects from outside

Most of these were settled slowly and against initial instinct. Anything that reopens one will burn hours reaching the same place.

5.1 One coefficient, everywhere. Krippendorff’s alpha in both functions, under the same level argument. Cohen’s kappa is gone. A kappa on one side and an alpha on the other cannot be compared, and kappa is nominal-only so it carries on an ordered scale the exact defect the ordinal metric removes. Measured on three real corpora, the two differ by at most 0.002, so nothing was lost.

5.2 No invented thresholds. Ever. The literature supplies cutoffs for alpha and none for the diagnostics. That absence is kept, not filled. A cutoff a package author asserted has none of the authority a field-agreed convention has, and it is the easiest thing in a manuscript for a reviewer to attack. This rule has killed a required-N helper, an aspect-ratio warning, and two others.

5.3 The cutoffs govern a different decision than validate_sample() asks. Krippendorff’s bar answers whether codings are clean enough to analyze, which assumes two humans implementing one codebook. validate_sample() asks whether a model is doing what a coder does, which has no fixed answer and whose reference is a measured human ceiling. The coefficient transfers. The bar does not. Alpha was nearly removed from validate_sample() over this. It stays, with landmarks rather than a cutoff. Zero is the class mix, one is every row, and there is no third landmark because a third would be the rate two people reach and nobody has measured it.

5.4 Retired, there is one basis. The draw gives every pair the same chance, so the figure on the coded rows is the corpus figure, and the sample and corpus rows this entry ranked went with the tilted draw. See 5.30.

5.5 The ceiling is not the benchmark. coder_agreement() is internal and builds $ceiling. Its job is getting the hand coding into shape. Which coder is out of step and which question is contested. The drawn sample is the right population for that, since the coding is the subject. The benchmark reading lives in $gap.

5.6 Retired with the weights. Nothing passes weights to kripp_parts() or prf() now, so the normalization and the argument are gone. See 5.30.

5.7 Prose rule. No sentences that reassure by stating the obvious. Not “that is a finding rather than a failure,” not “this is normal rather than an edge case,” not “X is still interpretable.” State the fact and stop. No em dashes, no colons in prose, American spelling, no contractions. Applies to roxygen, console messages, vignettes and code comments.

5.8 Numbers in documentation must be derived or cited. No figure appears in a help page unless a reader can see where it came from. The rule reaches the document as well as the help pages, since a figure here with no derivation beside it decays the same way, which is what the test counts in 2 are maintained against. In an article, every figure in a sentence comes from inline R, so a re-render cannot leave the prose behind.

5.9 @references blocks are alphabetical by first author. Standing.

5.10 Naming. (all items) for the pooled row in every table that pools. $gap rather than a name asserting a ceiling, because models sometimes exceed the human figure and a name asserting they cannot would be false in a case the table shows.

docs rather than texts for the document frame, in inspect_cases() and coding_sample(), and for the attribute measure.character() stashes. The frame holds documents of any kind, the examples already called the variable docs, and texts beside a text column made the same word mean two things.

The attribute was argued for keeping, on the grounds that it holds character strings and only the character method writes it. That argument loses to one line. as_docs() accepts a character vector of documents under the name docs at utils.R:295, and returns the same tibble the stash branch returns twenty lines above it, so one function was using two words for one thing. Names here follow the role, as prob_renorm, prob and prob_other do, rather than whatever the object currently contains.

texts survives in context.R, where the parameter is a character vector of document text used for word counts and prompt sizing, and where 9.2 sends media into the measuring call beside it. There the word is accurate.

5.11 Retired with per-category alpha. $categories carries precision, recall and AUC for every label instead. See 5.12.

5.12 Precision, recall and AUC come for every label. One row per label per question in $categories, each label against the rest, so no target is needed and nothing comes back NA for want of one. A label the model never chose has no precision rather than a precision of zero, since the question was never put. There is no pooled row, since a label pooled across questions ranks documents from one question against documents from another.

5.13 The soft path scores with Brier, not cross-entropy. score.R gives an absent label exactly zero, pinned by a test, so prob_renorm reaches the boundaries and the log score returns infinity. The forecasting literature says to prefer a bounded rule where forecasts can legitimately reach 0 or 1, and clipping hides an undeclared constant.

5.14 Retired with the design columns. The sheet no longer carries drawn_n, since only the corpus row read it. See 5.30.

5.15 Failure severity follows a three-tier rule. stop() is a call that cannot be honored and the fix is in the caller’s arguments. warning() is a run that can proceed in a state worth knowing about. message() is reporting. A probe call the world did not honor is a warning, not a refusal, which is why a failed label probe warns and proceeds even under exact = TRUE.

The three counts are deliberately not given. They drift on any patch that adds a guard, and a figure in this document with no derivation beside it is the defect 5.8 exists to forbid.

5.16 auc_of() stays internal and the article reads the package’s own figure. Three definitions existed, fathom:::auc_of() plus one in the bake and one in example_nyt.qmd. Exporting it was considered and rejected. The defect is the second definition rather than where it lives, and an export is a CRAN interface commitment bought to solve a duplication problem.

What closed it is that the article never needed a copy. validate_sample() already computes that figure and prints it, since the instrument is two labels and the sheet is a census on one item. The recompute is deleted and the prose reads the auc column already on the page. The bake keeps its copy for the console reporting it does, which is one definition outside the package rather than two.

5.17 Settled recently, so do not reopen them. Items here about coder_agreement() and agreement_gap() as exported functions, the corpus row and n_eff describe the shape 5.30 retired, and stand as the record of why those were built. Each of these was asked, answered, and is a question a fresh reading of the code invites again.

There is no ati codebook and there never was. example_ati.qmd says so outright. The variables are named in the supplemental material with no account of how they were defined. The shipped ati is five columns, which is the whole of it rather than an interim state, and the vignette writes its own questions from the category names and Article 7 of the 2002 law for exactly that reason. Asking for the codebook wastes a turn and it happened twice.

The allowed column is not an unread column. It was filed for several sessions as a defect, on the reading that coding_sample() writes it and coder_agreement() never reads it, so users retype label ordering. Both halves are true and the conclusion is not.

allowed is a coder instruction. Its own comment at audit.R:1754 says so, that without it three coders return yes, Y and 1 and you find out at analysis time. It sits beside question, note and text, and nothing outside coding_sample() reads any of those four. A column written for a human and not read by code is doing its job.

And the retyping does not happen. labels_from_instrument() at validate.R:1861 returns names(sc)[order(sc)] from instrument$scores, both coder_agreement() and validate_sample() take instrument =, and the instrument travels on the results object, which is read as attr(results, "instrument") in ten places. You cannot reach the point of wanting an ordinal alpha without holding res, since validate_sample() requires it.

The one case with no instrument, sheets built from dataset columns as in complete_run.qmd, is also the case with no allowed column, so the proposed fix would not have helped it.

agreement_gap() asks for the metric rather than inferring it. coder_agreement() and validate_sample() both take instrument = and fall back through labels_from_instrument(). agreement_gap() does not, and the asymmetry is deliberate.

It consumes two already-computed objects rather than sheets, and it recomputes alpha from $coded, so it has to be told the metric. Neither input records what it was built with. So an instrument = argument would let a run built under "nominal" be scored under "ordinal" from a scores vector that had nothing to do with it, and nothing could catch the mismatch. That argument would look authoritative and be silently wrong. Typing labels makes the scale a choice the caller made rather than one the function guessed, which is 5.2 applied to an interface.

The only safe improvement is the larger one, where validate_sample() and coder_agreement() stamp their metric and labels onto their returns and agreement_gap() reads them and refuses on disagreement. That is the 5.14 shape and it is an enhancement rather than a repair.

That improvement was built the other way round. Stamping and refusing is a check, and it leaves three calls a reader has to keep in agreement. Passing a named list of sheets to validate_sample() makes them one call, and the mismatch is then unrepresentable rather than caught. The several-sheet path in 4 has the shape.

The stamping half survives for the design and only for it, since coding_sample() writes that onto the sheet and neither this function nor its caller invents it. The metric is different because a metric is a reading a caller chooses and a design is a fact about a draw that already happened. agreement_gap() still asks for the metric and the labels, and still should.

A failed label probe under exact = TRUE warns rather than refusing, and the refusal happens one step later. 5.15 puts a probe the world did not honor in the warning tier, and check_backend() then declines the instrument outright by reading exact_match against firsts. That costs no call and has no false positive, since exact = TRUE is refused without a backend and firsts is written only where the probe returned every label.

What stays uncovered is a probe that came back and separated the labels badly. Catching it means eliciting each label in turn at measure time, which is probe_labels() run again, and its result needs a person to read, since a token that is not a prefix covers a tokenizer split and a model disagreeing with the probe document equally. Left alone deliberately.

index.md names every export but one. read_checkpoints() is omitted on purpose, and check_backend() has been internal since 9.9. The page reads as an abstract, the omitted export is covered in quick_start.Rmd and the reference index, and naming every export would cost the register. Everything else on that page was corrected and nothing about it is outstanding.

README.md is not index.md and the two answer different questions. They were briefly identical, deliberately, so that one could be cut down from the other. index.md is the landing page of a site whose reference index is one click away, so a function catalog there is an outline of what the reader is about to browse. README.md is the front of a repository, read by someone deciding in thirty seconds whether to keep reading, and a catalog of twenty functions is the wrong thing to hand them.

So the catalog goes and a worked run replaces it. Two blocks, one measuring a corpus and one validating it against a coder, which is the whole shape of the package in about forty lines. The claim about reading a distribution stays, since it is the reason to look at all. Installation stays verbatim. Everything else compresses to links, and those are absolute, because quick_start.html resolves under pkgdown and is a dead link on GitHub. Half the bytes.

No output is printed in either block. The numbers would come from one model on one day, nothing regenerates them, and 7.4 is the rule against writing a figure from a description of it. The prose says what comes back instead.

The badge row goes above the image when it is written, and nothing here occupies that space.

That plan was not kept. README.md now carries the step outline index.md carries, in shorter form, and no worked run.

keep_alive stays at 24 hours. The default suits a corpus run over one model, which is what the package is written around, and the loop case is named in @param instead. The package’s answer to a setting that bites is to detect and report, which is what check_backend() is.

check_backend()’s guard counts rather than pairs by name. Nine documented \item labels against nine return(FALSE) paths, plus each path carrying a message(). The labels are prose and the messages are different prose, so nothing pairs textually without a marker convention the package does not have. A renamed failure is what this misses, and closing that costs a tag beside every return.

Retired with the weights. n_eff was added to $calibration to match its @return, and both went with the weights in 5.30.

The decision table left with interpreting-validation.Rmd, which was dropped for now. Its text has not been moved into any other document, and the test that held its six readings in place went with it.

5.18 Standing decisions inherited and still true. Prefix matching is the default scoring rule, with exact = TRUE plus backend as the escape hatch. Labels must differ at their first character, enforced at construction. prob_renorm is the measure and prob_other the diagnostic, which together recover prob (5.37). only= filters the return, not just computation. Checkpoint filenames carry an 8-character md5 digest. PABAK and the Stuart-Maxwell and Bhapkar tests are excluded, the first because it adjusts away a real property of the corpus and the second because significance is not the question.

5.19 The package version is recorded nowhere and printed nowhere. Six sites wrote or read it. stamp_provenance() stamped every validation object, new_results() stamped every results object, flat_results() carried the attribute onto the joined frame, measure() wrote it into every checkpoint payload, read_checkpoints() read it back, and the results header printed it beside the model, the ceiling and the run time. All six are gone, and the bake stopped saving it with them.

This reverses stamp_provenance()’s own stated reason for existing, which was that a figure queried a year later cannot otherwise be traced to a version. What replaces it is that the version is the weakest of the four things deciding a number. The model tag decides it, the instrument decides it, the call decides it, and all three are still stamped. A version pins the arithmetic, which is the part least likely to have moved between a figure being computed and a reviewer asking about it, and it cost a line on a header that already carries four fields.

Nothing on disk is invalidated. ckpt_stale() reads call_ok, model and prompt_hash off the stored frame and never looked at the version, so a payload written with the field is current and one written without it is too. read_checkpoints() stops looking rather than tolerating both.

Gorsky’s instruction, recorded because the absence otherwise reads as an oversight and the next reader puts it back. test-regressions.R pins it as a decision, on the attribute name and on the printed line, since renaming the attribute would satisfy a test written on the header alone.

5.20 Retired, the draw is uniform only. The tilted draw this entry defended, and uniform_share with it, are gone. 6.2 holds the measurements that showed what the tilt did to a ceiling, and 5.30 has why it went.

5.21 coder_reference() collapses several sheets into one, so validate_sample(coder_reference(ana, luis, bea), res) composes without a signature change.

majority writes the label most coders chose, and NA where two or more tie for the most, naming those rows on the console. A rule that broke the tie would invent a coding no coder produced.

unanimous writes the label only where every coder who saw the row chose it. It warns, because the rows it discards are the hard ones, so what survives is easier than the draw was.

soft writes (n_target + 1) / (n_coders + 2), Laplace-smoothed, so two coders who both said yes give 0.75 rather than 1. That is the honest reading of two observations, and it keeps the target off the boundaries, which matters because prob_renorm reaches exactly zero and a log score would be infinite there. It needs exactly two labels and refuses above two, since the honest soft target is then a vector of proportions and reporting one label against the rest would leave a two-category Brier beside a k-category one with nothing saying so.

A row only one coder saw has a majority of one and is trivially unanimous, which is why n_coders ships beside the label.

5.22 Intervals. ci = "none" by default, "bootstrap" to compute them, bootstrap_n = 2000L. conf_level sets the coverage of every interval, 0.95 by default. It is stamped on the result and stated under the first printed table that carries an interval, since the replicates are not returned and a caller has no other way to get another coverage afterwards. gap_ci is computed whatever ci says, since the gap is read through its interval.

The sample is a plain draw of units, so its interval is a plain resample of units, and every figure gets one. Percentile rather than normal-approximation, since alpha is bounded above by one and a symmetric interval runs past it wherever the coders agreed closely.

Intervals arrive as one bracketed character column per metric, placed immediately after the figure they belong to, and absent entirely under ci = "none" rather than present and full of NA. A column of NA reads as a computation that failed, and an absent column reads as a question nobody asked.

5.23 scale_reliability() was built, shipped and then cut on scope. Cronbach’s alpha and McDonald’s omega over the items of an instrument, with item-total correlations and alpha with each item dropped.

The line it fell on is as_wide(). That function is the handoff, and the page says so, ready for a measurement model or any other downstream analysis. Everything else in sections 4 and 6 asks whether fathom measured well. validate_sample() checks the model against people, and $gap checks whether the model disagrees worse than a coder does. This one asked whether the researcher’s scale is a scale, which is a question about the construct rather than about the measurement, answerable identically on hand-coded data, and the first thing psych or lavaan or mirt does anyway.

Its own implementation made the argument. omega_of() fitted factanal(factors = 1) to get its loadings, which is a worse version of the model a user reaching for alpha is about to fit properly, with fit statistics, in a tool built for it.

Two arguments for keeping it were considered and both fail on scope. That removal does not prevent the misuse, since a user will run psych::alpha() on the same frame and get the same number with the same problem, which is true and beside the point if the function should not be in scope regardless. And that reviewers expect alpha, which they do, from a user already in mirt where it costs one line.

What it would have needed to stay. Alpha on one model’s probabilities is not alpha on responses from people, since the classical justification assumes respondents, and the function said nothing about that. factanal() also returns a likelihood ratio test of whether one factor suffices, in fit$PVAL, and the function fitted the model and discarded it, so omega came back as a number computed under an assumption that was never checked. Both were fixable and neither was the reason it went.

5.24 Retired with the tilted draw. There is no tilt left to warn about. See 5.30.

5.25 Reasoning is off, and think is not an argument. Scoring reads generated position 1, and a model that reasons first puts something else there, so a setting with one legal value is not a setting. The constructor used to document think as always FALSE while storing whatever it was given. The argument is gone rather than guarded. The field stays FALSE on every backend, so the request body and every checkpoint still say so, and a DECISION test in test-regressions.R pins it.

5.26 modalities takes text, image or both. Those are what measure() can send. Audio and video reach the model as text and frames, through prepare_audio() and prepare_video(), so the two words named nothing the package sends and nothing read them. Naming either is refused with a pointer to those two functions, and a native path adds its word back when it sends one, which 9.7 gates.

5.27 A seed reaches its own call and nothing after it. coding_sample() called set.seed() on the session’s stream, so its seed decided every draw the session made afterwards, including the bootstrap of the next validate_sample(), whose intervals were reproducible by accident. local_seed() seeds for the length of the calling function and restores the session’s stream on exit, and nothing else calls set.seed(). validate_sample() takes seed = 1234L, the default coding_sample() already had, so the same inputs give the same intervals whatever ran before. NULL draws from the session’s stream instead. A list of sheets hands one seed to the ceiling, the gap and every per-coder call, so each part is reproducible on its own.

5.28 A call whose distribution held none of the labels has no winner. Every prob is zero on such a call, and slice_max() or which.max() handed the win to the first declared label in item_report(), inspect_cases() and validate_sample(). winning_rows() keeps no row for it. share_won divides by the documents scored on that question, so the shares of an item fall short of 1 by the share that answered outside the labels. validate_sample() sets such a coded row aside and says how many, the way coding_sample() never draws one and item_report() leaves such a document out of its renormalized figures. The test is on prob_renorm, which has no value on such a call, since prob and present left the results in 5.37.

5.29 Articles do not compare models with published benchmarks, with one deliberate exception. An article states what a researcher should do with their own results, and a benchmark figure goes stale with every model while inviting a reading the package does not make. example_nyt.qmd is the exception, because replicating Barberá et al. (2021) was its purpose from the start. It reports their published figures beside a row computed from its own run, on the same 420 segments, and states that the data are held fixed and the methods are not. The article was later dropped, so no article now compares against a published benchmark. See 5.32.

5.30 Validation reports what a researcher needs to move forward, and nothing beyond it. Validation is there to make a social scientist comfortable enough with the model’s coding decisions to move forward with them. quallmer’s comparison functions, which report coefficients and their intervals and nothing that decomposes them, were the guide, though not a template. What that cut, and why.

  • The tilted draw. Validating on the pairs the model found hardest describes the hardest slice, and people struggle on those pairs too. 6.2 records coder agreement near 0.4 in the least confident bins and near 0.85 in the most confident. A researcher who wants those pairs pulls them with inspect_cases(which = "uncertain") and codes them by hand. With the draw uniform the sample stands for the corpus, so the weights, the corpus row, n_eff, drawn_n, the survey interval and the boundary interval went with it, and survey left Suggests. The draw keeps its mechanics, so a seed draws the rows it always drew.
  • expected, bias and both tail probabilities. expected is alpha’s internal denominator, and under the ordinal metric it scales with the square of the pairable count, which took seven passages to fence. bias was Byrt’s index, carried over from kappa. p_below_zero is a one-sided bootstrap p-value the docs read as the probability of a hypothesis, and at 95 percent it decides nothing gap_ci does not. p_below and min_alpha went for the same reason.
  • $bins, $roc, $long, $coder_bins and $forecast. Two curves a reader can draw from $coded, a reshaped copy of the other tables, and two diagnostics of the tilt and the forced choice.
  • $categories carries precision, recall and AUC for every label, so target went. Precision and recall on a label are equal exactly when the model used the label as often as the coder did, which is the lean bias reported.
  • $calibration and $coded come back on request, through calibration and coded. Brier stays because a researcher who analyzes the probabilities needs to know they are honest, and AUC reads only their order.
  • $gap is one row per question, the model’s average alpha with the coders against the coders’ average alpha with each other. Which coder the model tracks more closely is still in $discrimination, one row per coder.
  • coder_agreement() and agreement_gap() are internal, since a list of sheets already returns the ceiling and the gap. coder_reference() stays exported, as the step that consolidates several sheets into one.

5.31 corpus_bias() and audit_abbreviations() were cut on scope. Both described the corpus rather than the measurement. corpus_bias() binned endorsement by length or another property and stopped there, since whether a difference matters depends on what the measure is for, and a rising rate cannot tell a model swayed by length apart from documents that say more as they grow. Separating those takes the researcher’s own covariates and model, which is the analysis as_wide() hands off to, and a regression version would carry the same confound while looking more authoritative. audit_abbreviations() counted capitalized tokens before any call, and the remedy for what it found is a definition in the instrument, which is advice rather than machinery. The NYT article’s length check, the ATI article’s abbreviation scan and the two FAQ answers built on them went with the functions. The prepare functions still return bytes, n_frames, n_pauses and the rest, so the check stays a few lines away for anyone who wants it. stopwords left Suggests, and stringi stays, since scoring and label folding use it.

5.32 example_nyt.qmd was dropped, because its reference cannot answer the package’s question. The package asks whether a local LLM can stand in for a qualitative coder, and answering that takes individual coders, a ceiling among them, and the gap. nyt_gold’s tone is not a coder. It is the sign of a crowd average over up to ten ratings, with only exact midpoints dropped, so alpha against it says whether the model reproduces a consensus, and there is no second coder to set a ceiling or a gap against. Krippendorff’s 0.667 and 0.800 were also set for coders who could stand in for one another. The run returned an alpha of 0.434 on 73.6 percent agreement, against chance agreement of 53 percent, the best of the methods the source paper compared, and the reason for dropping it would hold had alpha come back at 0.85. How the local LLM compares with crowdsourcing and supervised classifiers is a question for a paper rather than for the package documentation. nyt and nyt_gold went with it, along with their sections of the bake, and the help-page examples for item_report() and threshold_sensitivity() now read the parlasent run res_indep.

5.33 The FAQ was removed, and the ATI article and the bake were cut to what is read. The FAQ answered questions nobody had asked yet, so it returns when real ones arrive. The thirteen help pages that sent readers to it no longer do, and each keeps what it says about its own numbers. example_ati.qmd now builds one independent binary instrument and reads it with item_report(), as_wide() and threshold_sensitivity(). Its exclusive requester section went, since complete_run.qmd already builds an exclusive instrument, and its co-occurrence analysis went as downstream analysis rather than use of the package. The bake now saves only the three runs something reads, res_six, res_topics and res_indep. It no longer runs the ATI style and requester instruments, the parlasent label-constraint probes and forced choice, or the three-level comparison, which takes it from about 3,300 calls to about 1,800.

5.34 Arguments are named for a social-science reader. Renamed in October 2026, before any release. instrument(descriptions = ) became definitions, the word a codebook uses. metric became level in coding_sample(), validate_sample(), coder_agreement() and agreement_gap(), since nominal and ordinal are levels of measurement, and since validate_sample() also took an unrelated metrics. coder_agreement(q = ) became min_alpha, the bar it names. corpus_bias() took by for type and bins for n_bins, matching validate_sample(). measure(only = ) became items, matching coding_sample(). items itself stays, since a measurement instrument is made of items and the README points at item response theory. Objects built before the rename still read, through a fallback to descriptions and to the metric attribute. Since then coder_agreement() and agreement_gap() have gone internal, min_alpha has gone with 5.30, and corpus_bias() was cut in 5.31.

5.35 The run header gives values, not reasons. The Context line said how the ceiling was reached (as supplied, the floor, or 1.25x rounded up to a power of two), and the Longest doc line placed the document as 3635 of 286, which repeated the Documents line. Gorsky asked for the value alone, so the line is now Context Ceiling and gives the number, and the document goes by its id in quotes, as First token does. The one reason kept is (from the saved run), since a resumed run takes a ceiling the caller did not choose this time. The header’s values moved to HEADER_WIDTH, five spaces past its longest name. The progress line, the run summary and its retry tip start in the same column, and the bar went from 24 cells to BAR_CELLS, 15, so the line keeps its length.

5.36 item_report() keeps what the token-probability literature measures, and nothing that restates it. Decided in October 2026, after reading Wang et al. (2024), Licht et al. (2025), Halterman and Keith (2026) and Denney and DiGiuseppe (2026) against the package. endorse, n_endorse and mean_prob went, since what they carried was their gap from the renormalized pair, which is leaked mass read by subtraction. pct_extreme went because it cannot separate a decisive answer from one that never entered the label set. max_prob_other and other_vs_median became mean_prob_other, since a corpus maximum is set by one document and the ratio existed to make it comparable within an instrument, which a mean already is. min_top1 went because one answer’s confidence says nothing about an item, and n_endorse_renorm because it was a count behind a share.

n_off_label became pct_off_label, the form Halterman and Keith report legal labels in, and it now reaches the choice and scored shapes, which lacked it on exactly the instruments where a first token is most likely to miss. That is the exposure Wang et al. measure, first-token answers disagreeing with written ones. Under greedy decoding the written answer opens with the emitted token, so apart from variant pooling a disagreement needs an emitted token that is not a label.

pct_label_absent is new. Ollama returns at most 20 alternatives, so a label outside them scores exactly 0 and, on two labels, puts its partner at exactly 1, which pct_extreme_renorm cannot tell from the model’s own certainty. Licht et al. report the same truncation for GPT-4o, and Denney and DiGiuseppe show a model saturating with nothing truncated, so the two are read together and neither replaces the other.

The three columns describe calls rather than labels, so in the choice and scored shapes they repeat down the label rows, as mean_expected already did. The choice header lost its leaked-mass and winning-probability lines and the scored header its leaked-mass line, since leaked mass is a column now and the winning floor went with min_top1. n_failed counts calls with an error rather than failed rows divided by the label count. The function reads success as is.na(error) and no longer reads prob, present, top1_prob or call_ok, so nothing in it depends on those four columns.

5.37 The results keep nothing that what they keep already implies. Decided in October 2026 with 5.36. prob, present, call_ok, top1_prob and all_absent moved to DROP_COLS, so $probs is id, item, label and prob_renorm. prob is prob_renorm * (1 - prob_other) to floating-point precision and zero where no label appeared, which retires the sufficient statistic in 5.18. Licht et al. (2025) build their estimator from the same two quantities, the renormalized distribution and the mass on the answer tokens, and the one raw quantity in the literature read against the package, Plaut et al.’s confidence in the winning answer, is that same product for the winning label. present is whether prob_renorm is above 0, all_absent is prob_other == 1, and call_ok is is.na(error), which measure_one() now guarantees by giving every failure a reason. top1_prob recorded the mass a winning non-label held, which prob_other bounds.

All five are still computed and checkpointed, for the reason 2.4 gives for the rest of DROP_COLS. ckpt_stale() reads call_ok off the stored frame and the verbose line reads prob, so a checkpoint written on either side of this change reads the same, and re-running the bake reads its caches without a model call. Every reader moved to prob_renorm, which ranks the labels of a call in the order prob does, since every label is divided by the same total. threshold_sensitivity() lost value, which had one legal value once prob was gone, and 5.25 settled that such a setting is not a setting. as_wide() lost value = "prob" for the same reason, and $coded lost top1_prob.

The same mocked run, carrying a leak, a missing label, a call with no label and a failed call, returned identical item_report(), as_wide(), coding_sample(), validate_sample(), threshold_sensitivity() and inspect_cases() output before and after the change, apart from the columns that left.

5.38 The label order is tested by asking again. Decided in October 2026. Every call in a run sees the labels in the order the instrument declared, so a model that leans toward whichever label comes first leaves no trace in the run, however long it is. order_sensitivity() asks every document again, or a seeded sample of them, with the labels reversed and, on three or more labels, in one shuffled order that is neither. Those are the two reorderings of Test IV in Halterman and Keith (2026), who compare each with the original and also report Fleiss’ kappa across all three. Here each reordering is compared with the declared order on its own, since the declared answers are the ones the run reported. They are read off the results rather than asked again, which costs nothing and compares against what was actually reported.

The order moves where a prompt shows it, in the cue and in an exclusive instrument’s listing, and nowhere else. reorder_labels() carries matching, scores and probed tokens across by label name, so an audit cannot probe its way into a matching rule the run did not use. default_cue() and choice_listing() were lifted out of instrument() so the audit rebuilds both with the code that wrote them, and nine instruments built before and after the change came out identical, prompt hashes included. A cue written by hand is not rewritten. An instrument of items lists its labels nowhere else, so one with its own cue is refused rather than audited against its own prompt.

The instrument, the backend and the context ceiling come off the results, which makes an audit under another model unrepresentable rather than caught. Nothing is checkpointed. The prompt hash covers the cue and the label order, so a reordered call written to the run’s directory would mark the item stale and replace its rows.

Each order gets two figures. agreement and alpha compare the winning labels with the two orders as two coders, through the same kripp_parts() and level as validate_sample(). labels was added for the ordinal scale, beyond what was first agreed, because the parlasent six-level instrument carries no scores by design. Two more figures were tried and removed, prior_shift in 5.42 and mean_shift in 5.43.

A reordered call that fails or returns no label leaves n and is named in a warning, since an order that pushes the answer off the labels is itself an effect of the order and agreement cannot show it. A tie breaks on the first maximum in declared order on both sides, so it cannot depend on presentation. The pool is sorted by radix before the draw, so results read back from checkpoints draw the same documents as the object the run returned. n defaults to NULL, which asks about every document with a label. A number draws a seeded sample, and 50 puts the standard error of an agreement near 0.9 at about 0.04. A failed first call stops the audit, since a call fails only on the request or the payload and every later call goes to the same server and model.

5.39 The help pages say where the method stops, and the bake keeps one audit. Decided in October 2026. Three bounds from the literature read against the package are now on the help pages. instrument() says the exclusive form is the one to use when a document takes exactly one category or the categories are defined against each other, on the strength of Halterman and Keith (2026), who found no gain in preliminary experiments from asking about one category at a time and argue their codebooks need every category in view. It also says a label has to rank among the 20 first tokens Ollama returns or score exactly zero, and points to pct_label_absent. measure() gives the three known causes of a failed check before the first document, and the check’s own message now names the third. A model opening with prose has one published fix, worked examples in the question, which took Qwen3.8-27B from prose on 941 of 945 tweets to answers that could be scored in Denney and DiGiuseppe (2026). The fourth bound from the same reading, that a saturated expected_score ranks documents better than it measures the distances between them, was already on as_wide()’s help page.

complete_run.qmd gains a sixth step showing order_sensitivity() on the six-level run, over all hundred sentences, since a sample of 50 from a corpus that small leaves half of it unasked. The audit makes 200 calls and keeps no checkpoint, so the bake caches its result under the run’s prompt hash, marked all, and reads it on every later bake, and vignette_results.rds carries order_six beside the three runs. The step quotes the figures inline and says what agreement near 1 and shifts near 0 would mean, without saying which the run produced, since no bake has run the audit yet. The co-occurrence block left the bake’s console checks, since nothing read it once 5.33 cut the analysis it served.

5.40 An empty document can leave the model asking for one. Decided in October 2026, on the first bake with the audit, and overtaken by 5.42. Both empty-document calls checked on the six-level instrument came back with Please at position 1 and none of the six levels among the 20 alternatives, so prior_shift was NA with no word about why. A warning naming the token was added, and the bake over every document then found Please under all three orders. An empty column was the rule rather than the exception, which is why 5.42 removed it. Step 6 of complete_run.qmd reads its figures, which closed the item 5.39 left open, and 6.6 records them.

5.41 preview() returns what measure() sends. Decided in October 2026. preview() trims a long document at truncate and puts a bracketed line above the prompt when media travel beside it, and it used to return that same string. Its help page promised the string exactly as the model would receive it, which held only for a short text document. The return value is for diffing two prompts or quoting one in a paper, so it is now built from the whole document with no bracketed line, and only the screen is trimmed. The help pages, index.md, and README.md also say the string is the one sent before Ollama applies the model’s chat template, since fathom calls the generate endpoint without raw and Ollama wraps the prompt as the user’s turn.

5.42 prior_shift is gone. Decided in October 2026, after the bake over every document. The column compared the orders on a call with no document, to separate the order’s effect from the document’s. On the instruments the package is built for it never could. A question that refers to a document leaves the model asking for one, as gemma4:31b did under all three orders, so the column is NA on most instruments, and where it is not it rests on one call per order with no interval. No paper read against the package reports anything like it. It came from the content-free calibration of Zhao et al. (2021), which those papers cite. The empty-document calls, the warning 5.40 added and the column left together, which saves one call per order on every item, plus one for the declared order.

mean_shift stayed at this point, and 5.43 removed it as well. A signed pull toward the first-listed label, after Denney and DiGiuseppe’s position bias, and the change in expected level on an ordinal scale were discussed and not added.

5.43 mean_shift is gone too, so the audit reports winners only. Decided in October 2026. mean_shift was the mean total variation distance between a document’s two prob_renorm distributions, the flip rate carried from winners to probabilities. On answers that are all 0 or 1 the two are the same number by construction, since the distance between two such answers is 1 when they differ and 0 when they do not. In general mean_shift is the flip rate times the average shift among changed documents, plus agreement times the average shift among held ones. On the six-level run it sat at the flip rate, 0.250 against 0.25 and 0.232 against 0.23, and any model that answers with near certainty puts it there, so it repeated agreement in another unit. What remains is what Halterman and Keith report for their order test, the share of labels unchanged and a chance-corrected agreement across the orders, here Krippendorff’s alpha per pair to match validate_sample().

6. Evidence in hand

Verified against real corpora or by simulation. Use these rather than re-deriving. They are also the answer to the worry that low alphas make the package look bad.

6.1 Three runs, one model (gemma4:31b)

run n agreement alpha Brier
nyt relevance gate 60 0.833 0.593 0.329
parlasent sentiment 100 0.721 0.572 0.544
nyt economic tone 420 0.736 0.434 0.519

Two of the three runs are no longer in the package. The nyt rows left with their datasets in 5.32, and the parlasent sentiment row, the three-level forced choice res_sent, left with the bake trim in 5.33. The figures stay as the record.

The relevance row moved when the draw did, and not in the direction the tilt predicts. It was 0.890, 0.713, 0.383, 0.050 and 0.217 under the uncertainty rule, which was the only rule when it was computed. 0004 made the bake ask for design = "uniform" and the row above is the first uniform draw of it. Every figure got worse.

A tilt toward the rows the model was least decided about should make its figures worse rather than better, so the naive reading of that comparison is backwards. One pair of draws cannot separate a mechanism from a re-draw. The agreement difference is 3.4 documents of sixty, the row rests on sixty of a hundred either way, and the nyt relevance instrument is saturated at pct_extreme_renorm above 0.9, which leaves the tilt little to tilt on. The honest position is that both numbers are recorded and neither explains the other, and a forty-seed scatter on this corpus would settle it.

The other two rows are censuses and did not move.

The coefficient orders the tasks the way anyone who knows them would. That is the strongest available evidence the measurement works. A coefficient reading the same everywhere would be the thing to worry about. None of the three now clears Krippendorff’s tentative bar, where the relevance run did at 0.713, so the presentation strategy is the range and what moves it rather than a bar.

Alpha against kappa on all three gives gaps of 0.000, 0.002 and 0.001. Both ladders place all three in the same band. This is why kappa was removable at no cost. The honest way to give a reviewer the familiar anchor is to say alpha agrees with kappa to three decimals here, and why, rather than saying they are the same thing. They differ by how the chance baseline is pooled, and the gap grows as the two coders endorse at different rates.

parlasent $categories against the reconciled code runs Negative 0.742, Neutral 0.505 and Positive 0.463, on marginals of 61, 66 and 73. With target = "Positive", precision 0.524 against recall 0.727. The model reaches for Positive too readily, which is a specific fixable finding about one label’s description.

6.2 The parlasent human ceiling, settled

The two annotators, before reconciliation, over the hundred sentences:

reading n agreement alpha
six levels, nominal 100 0.570 0.480
six levels, ordinal 100 0.570 0.701
three levels 100 0.720 0.579
two levels, negative or not 100 0.840 0.655

The 0.480 came from the metric, not from the annotators. Of the 43 disagreements, 20 are one step apart, and the nominal metric charges a one-step miss exactly as much as Negative against Positive. The ordinal reading is 0.701, which clears Krippendorff’s 0.667.

Per-category on the six levels shows the disagreement is not uniform:

M_Negative  24  0.340       Negative   48  0.509
M_Positive  22  0.289      N_Neutral   37  0.505
                           P_Neutral   36  0.528
                            Positive   33  0.603

The two mixed levels carry it. That puts a coefficient behind a claim data.R already makes as raw rates, 0.765 on the four unambiguous levels against 0.625 on the two mixed.

Every figure below reproduced on a cache-deleted re-bake, with every model call re-run from nothing and the parlasent block rewritten from five calls to one per metric. Both checks at once. The pipeline is deterministic under re-measure, so a moved figure in this section is a real change rather than noise, and the one call computes what the five did.

The comparable pair. Scored against each annotator separately, on the same rows and unweighted:

pair agreement alpha
model vs annotator1 0.720 0.581
model vs annotator2 0.690 0.536
annotator1 vs annotator2 0.720 0.579

The model sits at the human figure on one pairing, 0.581 against 0.579, and below it on the other. A 0.002 gap on 100 units is one document, so the honest reading is indistinguishable on annotator1 and below on annotator2.

The gap puts a number on that reading rather than leaving it to the eye. From the bake, on the six-level ordinal reading where the ceiling is 0.701, the model’s alpha is 0.770 against annotator1 and 0.697 against annotator2. Measured one coder at a time, as the gap was then, the two came to 0.0693 with an interval of [-0.07, 0.20] and -0.00415 with [-0.14, 0.14]. On three levels, ordinal, against a ceiling of 0.617, they came to 0.0211 and -0.0269.

One gap pointed each way at both granularities and no interval excluded zero. The model sits about where a second coder sits and a hundred sentences cannot separate them, which is the answer rather than a failure to find one. The gap now averages the model’s alpha over the coders, so on six levels its point is (0.770 + 0.697) / 2 - 0.701 = 0.0325.

The averaged gap, recorded by the bake after 5.33. model_alpha 0.733 against coder_alpha 0.701, a gap of 0.0326 with an interval of [-0.09, 0.15] on 100 sentences. The 0.0001 against the hand figure above is rounding in the two alphas it was built from. The interval spans zero, as both one-coder intervals did, so the reading above stands. Every other figure in this section came back unchanged, since the run read its checkpoints and made no calls.

Coder agreement against the model’s own uncertainty, ten equal-count bins of ten, was the first and last real-data reading of $coder_bins, which 5.30 removed.

0.3  0.4  0.4  0.5  0.3  0.4  0.9  0.7  0.9  0.9

The premise the tilted draw rests on holds, and it is a step rather than a gradient. Agreement sits near 0.4 across the bottom six bins and near 0.85 across the top four, with the break around a winning probability of 0.99999. Below that the model’s confidence carries almost no information about how hard a sentence was, and above it a great deal.

Do not compare the model’s figure against the reconciled code to the annotator ceiling. Those are 0.710 unweighted and 0.721 weighted against a ceiling that is unweighted and between annotators. Agreeing with a cleaned consensus is easier, the weighting is on one side only, and the comparison would credit the reconciliation to the model.

The marginals say where the difference comes from. The model puts 40 documents in Positive, annotator1 puts 33 and annotator2 puts 22, and annotator2 is the Neutral outlier at 42 against annotator1’s 31.

Forty seeds per design settle what one seed could not. Twenty coded rows drawn from the hundred, forty times under each design, against a census ceiling of 0.701 and a census gap of -0.004 on the second annotator.
