Two claims in this section were falsified by those files rather than by review, the compute type and the diarizer version, and one defect only the parakeet file could find.

read_timings() subsetted by name without checking it had a named list, so a shape with no word objects anywhere raised a subscript error instead of reaching the refusal written to describe it. The refusal was correct in intent and could not be delivered. Both pull() and the guard now test is.list(x) and nm %in% names(x) first.

The whole point of asking for real output rather than writing to a description is that all three of those were invisible to reading.

9.5 Notes that outlast the build

Two setup notes worth keeping, both found the hard way. uv tool install whisperx rather than uvx whisperx, since the refusal checks Sys.which() and the ephemeral runner puts nothing on PATH. And R does not always inherit the PATH a shell uses, so a recognizer that answers in the terminal can be invisible to Sys.which(). The refusal names that before it names installation, because the first version sent Gorsky to reinstall something he already had. The fix is PATH=${PATH}:/your/dir in ~/.Renviron, which also covers Rscript and check() where a Sys.setenv() line would not.

A native audio path exists and is deferred, not dropped. 9.7 has what was measured and what would gate it. It is a post-release addition rather than part of the first version.

9.6 prepare_video(), and what choosing frames turned out to involve

Most of it was already built. 9.1 settled that a frame reduces to an image and the multi-image probe settled that several in one call cost linearly, so measure() needed nothing. The audio half is prepare_audio() unchanged on a wav ffmpeg extracts. What was left was choosing which frames.

ffmpeg scores every frame and the score needs no threshold. select='gte(scene,0)' keeps every frame where the usual gt(scene,T) throws the number away and keeps a boolean, and metadata=print writes lavfi.scene_score for each. A threshold on that score would be a claim about where scenes begin, which is what removed window. Keeping the scores makes the question a ranking rather than a cutoff.

Verified on a synthetic file with cuts at 3, 6 and 9 seconds. The three highest scores landed exactly on them at 0.70, 0.89 and 0.64 against a next-highest of 0.011.

The scores come off the log rather than out of a file. metadata=print with file= put a temporary path inside the filter string, and a Windows drive letter ends the option at its colon. With no file the filter writes the same two lines per frame to the log, each behind its tag, and scene_lines() keeps only the tagged lines, so a line printed from elsewhere in ffmpeg cannot land between a frame and its score. Read off ffmpeg 9.0.2 output, where a twelve second file with cuts at 3, 6 and 9 seconds returned the same 120 scores both ways.

Scoring is free, which removed an argument. 5750 frames of a four minute video scored in half a second, roughly 480 times real time. A downscaled pass correlated at 0.9998 and picked the same frames, so the coarse-pass fallback that motivated a scale argument is unnecessary.

But "uniform" is the default, and not on performance. A rule that picks where the picture moved has decided that visual motion is where the evidence is, which suits a question about violence and works against one about setting. Choosing frames by what you expect to be asked is interpreting before the model sees anything, and it is the same objection that removed window and the per-word acoustics. Even spacing asserts nothing.

The literature agrees for its own reasons. Frame-sampling benchmarks standardize on a fixed count sampled evenly to guarantee coverage start to end and avoid bias toward specific parts of a recording, and uniform is the strongest baseline where the answer could be anywhere. Adaptive selection beats it by one to four points, inconsistently, and most on long videos. Every strong adaptive method is query-conditioned, which is exactly the part unavailable here.

A-PACK is worth reading and mostly unusable. Its measured asymmetry is real, audio carrying higher per-token importance and diversity than video, which is the argument for a frame-light corpus beside a full transcript. Its segment scoring and inner-LLM pruning are built on query relevance and cannot be taken.

frames is fixed across the corpus and gets a default where pause did not. A rule giving one recording twelve frames and another three would confound the count with whatever is measured. The default is defensible because it asserts only what you are willing to spend, not where evidence lives. Cost decisions can have defaults and measurement decisions cannot.

There is no derivable optimum. Accuracy against frame count rises and then falls, and where it turns is a property of the model and the corpus. The answer is the one threshold_sensitivity() already gives for cut points, which is to run the instrument at several values and read where it stops moving.

min_gap is load-bearing and its first value was wrong. Without it, seven of eight frames landed in the last forty seconds of a four minute video, because one busy stretch takes the whole budget. duration / (2 * frames) fixed that and introduced another. It lets every frame fit inside a fifth of the recording, and once the real peaks are used every remaining score is within a hundredth of every other, so the walk becomes index order and takes the earliest frames. On the twelve second fixture it put four of eight in the first two seconds.

duration / frames is the value with a statement behind it, that no two frames sit closer than an even sample would put them, which makes "change" a perturbation of "uniform" rather than a free choice. A gap that wide can exhaust the candidates before the budget, so the shortfall is filled at the midpoint of the widest space left. That needs no threshold and it makes "change" with no scores return exactly what "uniform" returns, which is the right answer for a recording ffmpeg could not score.

include_first spends a frame rather than adding one. Frame zero has no predecessor and scores exactly zero, so "change" can never reach it, and on the test corpus the opening shot was an object establishing what the scene was about. It has to be reachable and it has to not change n_frames.

A silent recording is a document. ffprobe is asked before anything is extracted, because ffmpeg errors rather than writing an empty wav when there is no sound track. The row comes back with frames, has_audio = FALSE and every audio column NA, and the count is reported. That row is the one a missing file gets except for exists, since naming a tool and a model on a recording never transcribed asserts settings that produced nothing, which is the same lie removed from a cached transcript and from one with no record. A batch of forty advertisements does not stop because three are silent. exists and has_audio answer different questions and NA on the second means the file was never opened.

n_words is NA there rather than 0. Nothing was transcribed, which is not the same as a transcript that came back with no words in it.

Frames live beside the recording, not in tempdir(). measure(image = ) reads paths, so three things break otherwise. coding_sample(copy_media = TRUE) copying media beside a sheet, a corpus saved and reloaded in another session, and the cache, which is pointless if what it points at is gone.

And prepare_video() calls prepare_audio() rather than the reverse. A video is a different kind of document from a recording, and 9.2’s rule is that helpers return objects and never perform hidden steps. Two functions with one calling the other keeps each one’s refusals about its own arguments, and the transcript cache works unchanged because the wav lands beside the video.

The frames keep a record of their own. <stem>_frames.fathom.json in the frames directory holds the times the frames were cut at and the JPEG quality. A file name says only which frame of the set a picture is, so before the record a second call under other settings kept the old pictures while frame_times reported the new times. A set cut under anything else, or with no record, is removed and cut again, which costs one ffmpeg call per frame and never touches the transcript. ffprobe is found beside the ffmpeg in use, then on the PATH, and refused when neither has it.

9.7 The native audio path, measured and deferred

9.1 concluded that Ollama does not take audio and that was one endpoint too wide. It tested /api/generate with fields named audio and audios, correctly found both discarded, and generalised. The route is input_audio on /v1/chat/completions, which 9.1 never tried. A ComfyUI node claiming Ollama sniffs RIFF headers in images[] is what prompted the retest; that specific claim is false and returns invalid image input, but chasing it found the gap.

Five conditions were measured on gemma4:12b and all five hold.

The model declares audio in /api/show. input_audio returns 200 where a field nothing reads returns 400, so a 200 means routing rather than tolerance. reasoning_effort = "none" puts a digit at position 1 where the default puts <|channel> at 0.993, which is the case check_backend() was rebuilt to catch. Four identical calls give a shift of exactly zero, so the server is deterministic and any difference at all is signal. And two recordings separate by 0.489 against that floor of nothing.

recording A   '2'  2=0.375  1=0.259     two speakers, correct
recording B   '1'  1=0.748              one speaker
no audio      'Please'  0.900

The silence arm is the important one and it reverses 9.1’s shape. On /api/generate a missing recording produced a confident answer about audio the model never received. Here it produces a request for the audio. The failure mode is honest on this endpoint, which is worth more than the separation number.

And Google’s own modality advice is wrong here. The Gemma 4 card asks for audio before text. Audio last separates the recordings almost twice as well, 0.950 against 0.489, and is more confident on the correct answer, 0.936 against 0.375. Documented and measured disagree, and 7.4 says which one wins.

None of this touches accuracy. On the same clip e4b answered one speaker where 12b answered two, and the clip has two. A model that hears is not a model that is right.

It is deferred because the library has one family in it. gemma4 is the only entry on Ollama’s popular listing carrying an audio badge, and the sidebar has no audio filter to find others with. Google’s own table puts a ~300M audio encoder on E2B and E4B and prints No Audio against 31B Dense, so this is not a packaging gap that a rebuild fixes. nemotron3 describes audio understanding and speech transcription in prose and ships badged vision tools thinking. Ollama’s per-tag lines say Text, Image for every Gemma tag including the ones that have audio, so /api/show on the running server was the only source that matched reality.

So the native path runs on a 4B-effective model with a 300M encoder, against a transcript path that runs on any of the thirty-three models installed here including a 31B and a 35B. That is the argument for shipping the transcript path first and adding the other later, and it is about availability rather than about which is better, which nobody has measured.

What it would ship as is a fork, not a replacement. prepare_audio() unchanged, and beside it a route where measure() puts the question to the recording with nothing in between. 9.2 spends four paragraphs on the representation choice a transcript forces; the second route does not make that choice, and both being available is what lets the two be compared.

And it would be gated by a check, not a model list. A compatibility list would be inference from a sample of one and wrong within a month. The five conditions above are a runtime test each server answers for itself, which works on a model neither of us has seen. It is check_backend()’s job pointed at a different endpoint, and the refusal it produces prevents exactly what 9.1 found, a fluent answer to a recording that never arrived.

Two things would have to be settled before it is written. num_ctx is not settable on the compatibility endpoint and Ollama’s documentation says to use a Modelfile, which resolve_num_ctx() exists to avoid. And build_prompt() produces one string where that endpoint takes a messages array, so the prompt differs, prompt_hash differs, and nothing cached transfers between the two routes.

The experiment that decides whether it is worth building is one corpus measured three ways, transcript alone, transcript with markers, and native audio, read against each other with the gap validate_sample() reports. Framed honestly that is a 4B model listening against a 31B model reading, and the transcript path wins on every axis except one.

9.8 The listing says what each model accepts

ollama_backend() with no model now prints a modality column, so choosing a model and learning whether it takes pictures are one step rather than two.

gemma4:26b      18.0 GB   25.8B Q4_K_M   text, image
gpt-oss:20b     13.8 GB   20.9B MXFP4    text

It costs one call per model and only on the discovery branch. /api/tags carries the name, size and quantization and not the capabilities, so this is a second round trip each. That branch is interactive, errors immediately afterwards, and is the moment a caller is choosing, which is the only place the cost buys anything.

A first failure abandons the rest. A server answering /api/tags and not /api/show would otherwise pay one timeout per model, so it pays one. Later failures are skipped individually, since by then the endpoint is known to work.

Only text and image are named, and that is a decision rather than an omission. The server also declares audio, tools and thinking. measure() builds its want vector from text and image alone, so naming anything else would invite a call that fails later rather than at the point of choosing. audio in particular is declared by two models here and 9.7 records why the package cannot send it.

The words are measure()’s, not the server’s. Ollama says vision where the package says image, and the listing prints what a caller would type into modalities. modality_words() is that translation and is a pure function, so the mapping is testable without a server, which the rest of this is not.

And the first version paid that cost three times. ollama_tags() is called by the listing branch, by the model-validation branch, and by check_backend(), which measure() runs before every corpus. Putting the fetch there meant ollama_backend("gemma4:31b") and every measure() call paid one request per installed model, thirty-six of them on the machine this was written against, on runs that print no listing at all. The roxygen said it ran only on the discovery branch, which was an assumption about the call graph rather than something read from it, and is the same failure 7.4 records twice already. The fetch is in show_models(), which is the only path that prints.

A tibble is not a data frame here. The first version guarded the absent column with tb$modalities %||% ..., which returns the fallback and warns on the way, because tibble reports an unknown column where a data frame returns NULL in silence. The guard asks whether the name is in names(tb) instead, and the test asserts silence rather than only the output.

What it does not do is set modalities. That argument is still a declaration the caller makes, and ollama_backend() does not read the server to fill it. Doing so is worth considering, since a declaration checked against the server would catch a typo that currently surfaces as a refusal from measure(), but it changes the meaning of an existing argument and is not part of this.

9.9 check_backend() is internal

It was exported and is not any more, and its own signature settled it.

check_backend(backend, instrument = NULL, num_ctx = NULL, text = NULL, ...)

use_own <- !is.null(text) && !is.null(instrument)

Everything but the backend is optional, which was the argument for exporting it. A caller could test a model in one line with no instrument and no corpus. But without both, the function builds a generic YES/NO instrument and probes with that, so the convenient call tests whether a model puts something label-shaped at position 1 for a question the package invented. measure() passes the real instrument and a real document, so the automatic check is strictly stronger than the manual one, and the export’s whole convenience was that it tested less.

And nothing is lost by removing it, because the check already runs before the corpus loop, so a refusal costs one call and no documents. Someone wanting to try a model before committing writes measure("test", ollama_backend(m), ins), which is one line and tests the real labels.

Gorsky’s argument, which is the one that holds. The package has safeguards for exactly this and they run on their own. A separate function to invoke them by hand is a second way to do what the first way already does, worse.

What survives is the explanation rather than the function. The paragraph in quick_start.Rmd about why position 1 matters and why the refusal exists is the most useful prose on that page, and it now attaches to the probe line measure() prints rather than to a call the reader can make. Three roxygen links pointed at [check_backend()] and are now backticked, since a @noRd block generates no topic. That check has caught the same mistake three times.

The vignette lost its last claim to running a model. Its intro said only one block called one, which was the check_backend() block, so after that left the count was zero. ollama_backend() reads /api/tags and /api/show without inference and prepare_audio() runs a recognizer rather than a model, so the sentence now says none of it sends a document to a model.

And its workflow list gained a step 0, matching index.md, because the page spends a hundred lines installing ffmpeg and a recognizer and then described a run in which neither appears. That step is also the only place either page says what the prepare_* helpers hand back.

It then fell a step behind at the other end. index.md carries a seventh step for threshold_sensitivity() and corpus_bias() and this list stopped at five, so a reader working from the page never learned those exist. The two lists mirror each other by design, and when one gains a step the other is where to look next.

Its <details> block is the control case for 0025. That one has opened and closed correctly since it was written, it holds a table and prose, and it contains no heading. The pattern was never the problem. A markdown heading inside one was.

One test read the block through @export. test-regressions.R finds the end of the @return block by looking for the next @export line, so that it can count documented failures against return(FALSE) paths. There is no @export after it any more, so the anchor is the definition instead. Nine and nine, as before.

9.10 The stems became four sets, one per medium

They all said text, and an image corpus was being asked about text that was not there. build_prompt() prints text_label only when there is text, so that half was never wrong. The stems were, on every medium but one.

Neutralising the noun was considered and rejected. document is the word the rest of the package uses and would have fixed the reference, but discuss and mention presume language whatever noun precedes them, so an image corpus would still have got a question about words. The fix is separate sets rather than a shared wording.

text   topic mention express about frame
audio  topic mention express about frame
image  show depict express about frame
video  show depict discuss express about frame

The sets are not translations of one another and that is the point. A picture mentions nothing, so image drops mention and gains show and depict, which Gorsky kept as separate stems because a photograph of a burning car shows fire and depicts a riot, and those are different measurements. video carries both plus discuss, since a row holds frames and a transcript at once and the verb is what says which channel the question is about.

CHOICE_STEMS follows the same nouns, two per medium, so 29 strings per language and 58 for the two.

medium has no default and is read only for a preset name. The sets differ, so a default would answer a question about the document with a guess. A literal question carries its own wording and needs none, which is what leaves every existing call that passes a question untouched. It reaches two functions rather than one, since template_items() reads ITEM_STEMS and instrument() reads CHOICE_STEMS on the exclusive path.

The refusals are separate and name what is wrong. A preset without a medium says the sets differ and lists the four. An unknown medium is refused before the lookup. A stem that exists for one medium and not another names the medium and lists what it does have.

The Spanish is written rather than converted. The demonstrative agrees with the noun, esta imagen against este video, which is why a {noun} slot was rejected before it was built. Four decisions in it are Gorsky’s rather than mechanical. depict is representa, which is the term in Spanish visual analysis. video is unaccented, the Latin American form, which the ati corpus already implies and which the file had never had to decide. The existing text stems move from El texto to Este texto, so that the four media read alike. And video’s discuss is trata sobre, the same phrase as text’s topic, with about still distinguished by principalmente exactly as it already was.

quick_start is the one vignette on the knitr engine. It moved from .qmd to .Rmd because pkgdown’s tweak_tabsets() finds tabsets with .//div[contains(@class, 'tabset')], a substring match, which grabs Quarto’s panel-tabset and rebuilds it as Bootstrap tabs with NA for every identifier. Quarto had built the tabset correctly and pkgdown destroyed it. R Markdown’s {.tabset} is the syntax pkgdown implements, so the file uses that. The other two vignettes compute and stay on Quarto.

VignetteBuilder carries knitr beside quarto for that reason. With quarto alone R CMD build enumerates only the engines those packages register, so a .Rmd is not a vignette at all and is skipped without an error. That is how it stood until a build_vignettes() run named three vignettes and the fourth nowhere, which is the quietest failure in this document and the reason the field is now a list. Every chunk in the file but setup is eval=FALSE, so building it needs no server.

tabset: true is set on the format, because html_vignette() defaults it to FALSE. That format exists to be small, around 10k where html_document() is 100k, so it ships a short stylesheet and neither Bootstrap nor jQuery. {.tabset} under it is a class attribute nothing implements, and the six #### children of ffmpeg and whisperx stack as ordinary subsections. Nothing is lost and the page is longer, which is the failure worth naming, because a reader sees a complete document and never learns that three of those sections were meant to be one.

It matters because two copies ship rather than one. build_site() writes docs/ and that is the web face. R CMD build writes the vignettes into the tarball, and that is what R-Universe serves, what CRAN links, and what vignette("quick_start", package = "fathom") opens with no site involved. The stacked version was the second of those, so the fix is not cosmetic. Both copies now render the same page.

html_dependency_tabset() is rmarkdown’s own implementation rather than Bootstrap’s. It supports navigation from the table of contents and from the URL, which the html_document version does not, and it does not support .tabset-fade or .tabset-pills, neither of which this file uses. Suggests gains rmarkdown (>= 2.13) because 2.13 is the earliest signature read off a source carrying the argument, which makes the floor possibly one release conservative and never wrong. An older rmarkdown fails on an unused argument rather than degrading quietly. pkgdown overrides output: with its own format and renders from the same source, so the site is unaffected either way.

Five languages follow this and not before it. Mandarin Chinese, Hindi, Modern Standard Arabic, Japanese and Korean. The first four are among the most spoken languages; the last two are there because Gorsky knows native speakers who can read them. Doing the media first means translating four nouns per language once rather than translating text and then re-translating it.

Eleven call sites had to change and a line-based sweep found none of them. Every one is a multi-line call, so a regex requiring the quoted stem on the same line as the opening parenthesis matched nothing. The first sweep reported nine hits, all of which were dismissed as false positives without being read, and the failure surfaced when example_ati.qmd refused to render. A sweep over this package has to balance parentheses and read the whole call, since almost every call in the tests and the vignettes spans lines. That goes in 7.3 with the other sweep rules.

And a preset cannot be verified by running it. all_absent was 0.00 across twelve languages and 3,600 calls, so the probe says the mechanism works whether the wording is right or subtly wrong. The check is a reader. That is the rule 7.4 already states about writing from a description rather than from the thing described, arriving in a place where no probe can substitute.
